newsitem.title: UK: Italy Dec fuel use for power falls 17.7 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Italy Dec fuel use for power falls 17.7 pct yr/yr.

text.p: Italy's consumption of high and low sulphur fuel oil for power generation was 1.70 million tonnes in December, a fall of 17.7 percent from December 1995, Italian industry data said on Wednesday.

Poor demand for fuel oil from Italian state utility ENEL, the world's largest single buyer of fuel oil, has helped knock over $25 a tonne off European fuel oil prices in little over a month, and contributed to a large build-up of unsold product in Europe in January.

Italian power stations consumed 17.52 million tonnes of low sulphur fuel oil and 4.83 million tonnes of high sulphur fuel during the whole of 1996, a 4.3 percent fall in fuel oil use from 1995, Italian trade grouping Unione Petrolifera said.

In addition to usage for power generation, Italy consumed 3.76 million tonnes of high and low sulphur fuel oil in 1996, 6.7 percent down on 1995, while December's consumption in this sector was 345,000 tonnes, unchanged from December 1995.
High sulphur consumption in the power generation sector fell by far more than low sulphur.
High sulphur consumption in this sector in December was 40.7 percent down year-on-year while consumption for the whole year was 15.2 percent down on 1995.
This compares with year-on-year falls in the low sulphur sector of just 5.0 percent for December and 0.7 percent for the whole year.
Total Italian consumption of high and low sulphur fuel oil in all sectors therefore calculates at 2.04 million tonnes in December and 26.11 million tonnes for the whole of last year.
Figures for total imports were not available, a source at Unione Petrolifera said, because ENEL had failed to provide recent data on changes in inventory levels.
Analysts and Italian industry sources said the decrease in fuel oil consumption was largely because of an ongoing programme to increase use of natural gas in Italy.
A secondary factor, sources said, was increased hydro electric production which was around seven percent higher in the last quarter of 1996 than in the same period in 1995.
